minutes.headline: Stormwater task force reviewed the ERU fee spreadsheet, fixed outliers, and prepared slides for Monday's library session.
minutes.summary: The task force went through the scrubbed ERU/utility fee spreadsheet, correcting blank use codes, a large quarry property, the Carousel Lane and Tri Town entries, and renaming a column to impervious area. They agreed the figures are a best-effort starting point open to review, planned to send the file to FinCom via a town contact but not post it online, and arranged a Friday Zoom to review slides before a Monday public session at the library. A roll call vote was taken to adjourn.

votes.motion: Motion to adjourn, moved and seconded, vote by roll call

budget_items.topic: Utility fee for the quarry property on Lunenburg-Shirley Road
budget_items.what_was_said: Calculated utility fee on the property's large ERU count was discussed as significant relative to its tax levy; left in place as open to review.
Consolidating the complex's impervious area gives a per-unit fee below a single-family home.
A member suggested showing 75% and 50% payment columns; others said abatements are a couple of years out and will be in the presentation.
The fee is expected near the stated level but is not final; the sum came over the sewer budget on purpose, and new permit requirements could raise costs.
Unpaid fees would go on tax liens, with delay of over a year and possible legal fees.

decisions.decision: Column header changed to impervious area; a note will say the spreadsheet figures are best effort and open to review.
Spreadsheet will not be posted online; it will be sent to a town contact to share with FinCom.
Tri Town entries to be zeroed, with a note that 37 Young's Road covers all of Tri Town.
Zoom review of slides set for 9:00 Friday among three members.
Library session meeting to be posted; scheduling of next meetings can be done offline.

Unpaid fees would go on tax liens, so a missed payment could carry a delay of over a year and possible legal fees.
